takeaway: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies cricothyroid, which controls pitch; injury in thyroidectomy loses high notes.

question.text: A singer cannot sing high notes after her thyroidectomy. What is the likely cause?
question.say: A singer complains of not being able to sing high notes following her thyroidectomy. What is the likely cause?

answer.text: Damage to the external laryngeal nerve
answer.say: The answer is damage to the external laryngeal nerve.

lines.text: A singer cannot reach her high notes.
lines.say: This singer cannot reach her high notes since her thyroidectomy.

lines.text: The thyroidectomy scar on her neck.
lines.say: Here is the scar of the thyroidectomy.
The cricothyroid muscle lengthens and shortens the vocal cords, and so controls voice pitch.

lines.text: The scissors threaten the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve, which supplies it.
lines.say: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies the cricothyroid, and here it has been cut.

lines.text: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is the other nerve at risk: hoarseness.
lines.say: The other nerve at risk is the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Damage to it causes hoarseness, not lost high notes.

lines.text: Remember: lost high notes after thyroidectomy mean external laryngeal nerve damage.
lines.say: Remember: lost high notes after a thyroidectomy mean damage to the external laryngeal nerve.
